evidence_snippets: “Six different serotypes have been identified based on the serological specificities of their polysaccharide capsules, with capsular serotype b as the predominant strain associated with invasive H. influenzae disease. Strains without capsules are referred to as non-typeable.”
“Vaccination against H. influenzae serotype b (Hib) was introduced in the 1980s…”

“In theory, vaccines that target only one serotype may drive the organism to either switch and/or replace their capsules with nonvaccine capsular types or shed their capsule altogether to become resistant to the vaccine.”
key_data_points: Hib vaccine targets Haemophilus influenzae serotype b only (serotype-specific coverage).
Haemophilus influenzae has six capsular serotypes (a–f); non-typeable strains lack capsule.
study_population: Invasive Haemophilus influenzae cases in British Columbia, Canada (2008–2009), children and adults (98 cases total)
